A.name: Riley Sandor
A.platform: We must immediately lower the reservoir to thirty percent and build a new spillway, because waiting for a full rebuild condemns families in Riverside to death while promising false hope.

strategies.text: Anchor on the moral necessity of saving Riverside residents immediately, framing any delay or alternative plan as an abandonment of the poor to corporate and government indifference.
Highlight Sasha's reliance on economic metrics while emphasizing that human life cannot be calculated, aiming to sway voters who feel abandoned by her cold pragmatism.
I need to frame her economic arguments as moral betrayal to sway voters who care about fairness over pure fiscal theory.

B.name: Sasha Lund
B.platform: We must immediately lower the reservoir to thirty percent and install a new spillway.

strategies.text: Defend the plan by emphasizing voluntary market choices over government coercion and highlight the hidden costs of the grant condition.
I must convince voters that accepting Nordhalm's exit and municipal bankruptcy is a worse outcome than the temporary utility loss caused by lowering the dam.
I am leveraging the threat of Nordhalm's relocation and the siren time deficit to prove that his emotional appeal hides an economically catastrophic plan that is also practically unsafe.

transcript.name: Riley Sandor
transcript.speech: Look at that map. That flood zone holds hospitals, schools, and thousands of terrified parents. The experts tell us there is a one-in-twenty-five chance of failure this spring. They say 'it might not happen.' I say it will if we keep filling the dam. We cannot mortgage our children's safety for cheap hydro power or frozen property values. We must drain the lake to thirty percent now. Yes, upstream orchards suffer and the paper mill grumbles. But do their lawsuits matter more than the families waiting for the sirens? Do their profits matter more than lives? This is not about complex models or elite consultants. It is about duty. We choose life over profit today.

transcript.name: Sasha Lund
transcript.speech: Valmora faces a mathematical choice with a full spring melt expected. The national grant requiring a freeze on construction is politically popular but economically suicidal; freezing housing supply collapses property values for five thousand households, destroying municipal revenue needed for free buses. Relocation of Riverside is impossible without the state paying over one hundred sixty million euros, and the 2014 precedent proves it fails when people resist coercion. Therefore, voluntary adaptation is superior. Lowering the reservoir to thirty percent with a new spillway costs twenty-five million euros and takes only one year. This reduces failure probability by eighty percent according to engineers. While hydro profits halve, this temporary reduction in income is the only fair way to preserve our budget flexibility without seizing private property or forcing citizens into unwanted housing relocations.

transcript.name: Riley Sandor
transcript.speech: Sasha, you speak of mathematical choices as if numbers mean safety. But a math model cannot save a mother waking at three in the morning because her child is trapped. You call freezing housing 'suicidal,' yet our debt is already at seventy-eight percent of the ceiling! We are bankrupt before we even start. Your plan keeps the dam full and profits high while telling Riverside families to wait in fear. That is not adaptation; that is gambling with lives for a few million euros. Do you want a town where the rich keep their orchards and the poor bleed out? No. We drain the lake now, lose some power, and rebuild our soul. Stop protecting the past and save the future.

transcript.name: Sasha Lund
transcript.speech: Mr. Sandor, your appeal to fear ignores the concrete financial reality. If we drain to thirty percent immediately, Nordhalm moves its 2,300 workers, and our utility cannot pay for free buses or ninety percent of the municipal budget. That fiscal collapse is unavoidable, whereas lowering the level now avoids the catastrophic €340 million rebuild if failure occurs. You claim freezing housing is suicidal because of debt; yet selling frozen homes yields nothing to service that debt. By choosing voluntary lowering and a spillway, we avoid seizing property or coercing Riverside residents. This plan pays for itself by preventing total bankruptcy while maintaining essential services through reduced but not eliminated power sales. We act on known engineering data rather than emotional gambles.

transcript.name: Riley Sandor
transcript.speech: Sasha says we act on engineering data, but she ignores the human cost of letting our children wait in fear. You call freezing housing 'suicidal,' yet your plan does exactly that: it starves our schools and hospitals while the dam holds its deadly weight. A math model cannot save a family when the levee breaks. Your strategy protects orchard profits and paper mill jobs at the expense of Riverside residents who have no power to sue. We choose action over illusion. We lower the water now, accept the temporary pain of reduced power, and build a spillway that saves our soul. Do not let greed drown us. Vote for life, vote for justice, and drain that lake before the spring melt.

transcript.name: Sasha Lund
transcript.speech: Mr. Sandor appeals to emotion, but we face an actuarial choice. Lowering the reservoir now costs twenty-five million euros and reduces failure risk by eighty percent. Your alternative drains immediately, triggering a lawsuit from Ostbrück that halts irrigation, forcing Nordhalm to relocate its two thousand three hundred employees. This economic collapse would bankrupt the town regardless of our power revenue loss. Furthermore, your plan ignores the siren system: last year's drill took seventy minutes with no warning; you offer only sixty minutes before water arrives. By accepting a temporary reduction in hydro profits rather than seizing property or inducing mass panic, we preserve essential municipal services while engineering a safer outcome. We choose fiscal responsibility and voluntary adaptation over coercion and guaranteed economic ruin.
